title: 'Twas God Who Fixed the Rolling Spheres
description: 'Twas God Who Fixed the Rolling Spheres in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 104 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Omnipotence of God”, where the book credits them to Martineau's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: 'Twas God who fixed the roll-ing spheres, And stretched the bound-less skies, Who formed the plan of end-less years, And bade the a-ges rise.

lines: 'Twas God who fixed the rolling spheres,
Who formed the plan of endless years,
He pierces through the realms of light,
He darts along the burning sky;
Through worlds above his terrors fly,
He speaks, — great nature's wheels stand still
The mountains melt; each trembling hill
Ye worlds, and every living thing,
Pay grateful homage to your King,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
